title: What is JSON?
description: In Depth Explaination of how JSON works

section-content: JSON stands for JavaScript Object Notation.
It is a lightweight data-interchange format used to store and transmit data between systems.
JSON is text-based, human-readable, and language-independent.
question-content.section-text: JSON uses key-value pairs. Keys are always strings wrapped in double quotes. Values can be strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, objects, or null.

solution-list.description: JSON works by organizing data into structured key-value pairs that can be easily parsed by programming languages.

thread.comment: How does JSON differ from XML?

replies.comment: JSON is more lightweight, easier to read, and uses less markup compared to XML. It also maps directly to objects in JavaScript and Java libraries like Gson or Jackson.

title: What is Polymorphism?
description: In Depth Explaination of how Polymorphism works in Object-Oriented Programming, specifically in Java.

section-content: In Java, polymorphism allows one interface or parent class reference to represent multiple different object types.
It enables flexibility, extensibility, and cleaner code design.
question-content.section-text: Polymorphism occurs when a superclass reference variable refers to a subclass object.

solution-list.description: Polymorphism allows objects to be treated as instances of their parent class rather than their actual subclass type.

thread.comment: Why is polymorphism useful in large applications?

replies.comment: It improves scalability and maintainability. For example, you can write code that works with a parent type (like Animal), and later introduce new subclasses (Dog, Cat, Bird) without modifying existing logic.
